title: The First Law of Complexodynamics
signal_engine_relevance: Frame transcript signals as patterns between randomness and over-simple keyword rules
Use compression-style diagnostics to spot boilerplate vs information-rich sections
future_features: Compression ratio feature for prepared remarks vs Q&A
core_idea: Complexity can rise and fall even while entropy rises monotonically; interesting structure may peak between order and randomness.
historical_importance: It connects thermodynamics, algorithmic information, and a practical intuition behind why the middle of a system evolution can be most informative.
beginner_takeaway: A sequence is not useful just because it is random or long; useful structure often lives in compressible-but-not-trivial patterns.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Compare compression/novelty scores against human evidence-span labels
Check whether high-complexity Q&A spans correlate with analyst pressure labels
risks_limitations: Conceptual blog post, not an NLP model
Compression proxies can confuse topic shifts with meaningful complexity

title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Recurrent Neural Networks
signal_engine_relevance: Motivates transcript-first sequence modeling before heavy architectures
Supports section-aware modeling of prepared remarks and Q&A
core_idea: Small recurrent models can learn surprising local and long-range structure from raw sequences.
historical_importance: It helped make sequence learning tangible and showed that raw text modeling could reveal structure without heavy feature engineering.
beginner_takeaway: RNNs process one step at a time while carrying a hidden state, so they are a natural first mental model for transcript sequences.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Train tiny local baselines only after enough transcripts
Evaluate generated/next-token probes as diagnostics, not product claims
risks_limitations: Blog/demo evidence is not domain validation
RNNs are mostly a historical baseline for modern transformer work

title: Understanding LSTM Networks
signal_engine_relevance: Clarifies why long earnings calls need memory over many turns
Gives vocabulary for modeling guidance setup and later Q&A follow-through
core_idea: LSTMs use gated memory to preserve and update information across long sequences.
historical_importance: It became one of the clearest explanations of why gated recurrent units solved practical long-dependency problems.
beginner_takeaway: The cell state is a controlled memory path; gates decide what to keep, forget, and expose.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Check whether later Q&A references earlier prepared remarks
Measure section-aware recall in retrieval baselines
risks_limitations: Tutorial, not a benchmark
Modern systems usually use transformers but still face memory-window design problems

title: Recurrent Neural Network Regularization
signal_engine_relevance: Warns that transcript models will overfit small corpora without disciplined regularization
Useful for 30/100/500 transcript model gating
future_features: Overfit warning report for optional classifiers
core_idea: Dropout can regularize LSTMs when applied to non-recurrent connections while preserving recurrent memory.
historical_importance: It made LSTM language models more reliable and practical across NLP, speech, translation, and captioning tasks.
beginner_takeaway: Regularization is not an afterthought; how it is applied must respect the model architecture.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Track train/dev gap by transcript count
Require held-out-call performance before promoting any learned model
risks_limitations: Small finance corpora are especially overfit-prone
Paper does not remove need for careful labels

title: Keeping Neural Networks Simple by Minimizing the Description Length of the Weights
signal_engine_relevance: Supports simple, auditable baselines before complex ML
Provides theory for penalizing over-complex transcript models
core_idea: A neural network should balance fit with the amount of information needed to describe its weights.
historical_importance: It is an early bridge between neural network regularization and information-theoretic model selection.
beginner_takeaway: A model that memorizes is expensive to describe; simplicity can be a guardrail against fake performance.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Compare simple deterministic features to optional learned baselines
Track performance per model-complexity tier
risks_limitations: Historical method, not directly implemented
MDL approximations can be hard to explain to nontechnical users

title: Pointer Networks
signal_engine_relevance: Maps neatly to evidence-span selection where outputs point back to transcript positions
Informs extractive citation-first interfaces
core_idea: Attention can act as a pointer over input positions, enabling variable-size outputs tied directly to the input.
historical_importance: It showed attention was more than soft context; it could select structured outputs from an input sequence.
beginner_takeaway: Some tasks should not generate labels from nowhere; they should point to the evidence that justifies them.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Evidence-span precision/recall
Reviewer agreement on selected transcript spans
risks_limitations: Do not claim neural pointer networks are implemented
Pointer ideas require gold spans to evaluate properly

title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
signal_engine_relevance: Sets expectations for data scale and benchmark rigor before multimodal claims
Useful historical anchor for future visual status/audio-video work
core_idea: A large CNN trained with GPUs and practical tricks dramatically improved ImageNet classification.
historical_importance: AlexNet marked the deep learning breakthrough moment for large-scale computer vision.
beginner_takeaway: Architecture matters, but the win came from model, data, compute, and evaluation all lining up.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Only evaluate visual features when source coverage and labels exist
Compare text-only vs text+media lift on fixed cases
risks_limitations: Image classification is far from earnings-call understanding
GPU-heavy training is out of scope now

title: Order Matters: Sequence to Sequence for Sets
signal_engine_relevance: Important for transcript chunks: some order is meaningful, some candidate sets need order-invariant treatment
Guides chunk ordering experiments
future_features: Permutation stress test for chunk rankers
core_idea: Sequence models can be sensitive to arbitrary input/output order when representing sets.
historical_importance: It clarified a subtle weakness in applying sequence tools to unordered objects.
beginner_takeaway: Before feeding data to a model, ask whether the order is real signal or an accidental artifact.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Shuffle candidate evidence spans and measure stability
Compare chronological vs relevance-sorted retrieval contexts
risks_limitations: Not a direct earnings-call model
Order invariance can remove useful chronology if applied carelessly

title: GPipe: Easy Scaling with Micro-Batch Pipeline Parallelism
signal_engine_relevance: Roadmap reference only: Signal Engine should scale data and evaluation before training large models
Informs future remote/GPU planning
core_idea: Large neural networks can be split across accelerators and trained efficiently with micro-batch pipeline parallelism.
historical_importance: It helped make model-parallel training more accessible for giant networks.
beginner_takeaway: Scaling systems work is valuable, but it only matters after the task, labels, and metrics are worth scaling.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Record cost/performance only after local baselines saturate
Gate GPU work on benchmark stability
risks_limitations: Out of scope for current repo behavior
Could encourage premature infrastructure work

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
signal_engine_relevance: Residual thinking maps to additive signal layers that do not erase deterministic baselines
Useful analogy for modular architecture
future_features: Residual-style model sidecars that preserve deterministic output
core_idea: Residual connections let very deep networks learn refinements over identity mappings.
historical_importance: ResNet made extremely deep networks trainable and became a backbone for vision and beyond.
beginner_takeaway: Sometimes the best module learns a correction to a reliable baseline rather than replacing it.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Ablate each sidecar as a residual contribution
Measure lift over deterministic baseline, not standalone score only
risks_limitations: Architecture analogy should not be overclaimed
Vision results do not prove transcript behavior

title: Multi-Scale Context Aggregation by Dilated Convolutions
signal_engine_relevance: Inspires multi-window transcript context features without losing local evidence resolution
Useful for hierarchical section/chunk analysis
core_idea: Dilated convolutions expand context without reducing resolution.
historical_importance: It influenced dense prediction models by showing how to aggregate broader context efficiently.
beginner_takeaway: A signal engine needs both the exact sentence and the surrounding call context.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Compare single-sentence vs neighboring-window evidence quality
Measure context window impact on false positives
risks_limitations: CNN mechanism is not directly used
Wide context can dilute evidence if not evaluated

title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
signal_engine_relevance: Maps to speaker-turn graphs, analyst/company interaction networks, and cross-call entity relations
Useful for future relational transcript intelligence
core_idea: Graph neural networks can be described through message, update, and readout steps over structured objects.
historical_importance: It unified several graph neural approaches and accelerated graph learning as a general framework.
beginner_takeaway: When the data is relationships rather than a flat string, graph structure can make the task clearer.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Evaluate graph features against Q&A friction labels
Ablate speaker/entity edges from retrieval
risks_limitations: Chemistry benchmark does not transfer directly
Graph construction can inject subjective assumptions

title: Attention Is All You Need
signal_engine_relevance: Core mental model for retrieval, reranking, long-context transcript analysis, and future transformer baselines
Guides attention-inspired evidence weighting
core_idea: Self-attention can replace recurrence/convolution for sequence transduction and scale efficiently in parallel.
historical_importance: The Transformer became the foundation for modern LLMs and most current NLP systems.
beginner_takeaway: Attention lets each token condition on other relevant tokens, but position and context design still matter.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Compare lexical retrieval vs embedding/reranker candidates
Measure evidence citation quality and section recall
risks_limitations: Do not imply a transformer is implemented here
Attention maps are not automatically explanations

title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
signal_engine_relevance: Directly relevant to aligning extracted signals with source transcript evidence
Pre-transformer foundation for evidence-aware modeling
core_idea: A translation decoder can softly search source positions instead of relying on one fixed-length context vector.
historical_importance: It introduced neural attention in a form that reshaped sequence modeling.
beginner_takeaway: For any output claim, the model should know where it looked in the input.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Gold evidence alignment precision
Long-section degradation tests
risks_limitations: Translation alignment is not identical to financial signal evidence
Soft attention is not a human-readable proof by itself

title: Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks
signal_engine_relevance: Architectural lesson for sidecars: preserve the base transcript object and add refinements
Supports non-destructive feature composition
core_idea: Clean identity paths improve optimization in deep residual networks.
historical_importance: It refined ResNet design and reinforced the importance of information-preserving paths.
beginner_takeaway: A system should keep a reliable path for original information while layers add value.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Verify sidecars never remove source evidence
Measure each layer as incremental lift
risks_limitations: Analogy only unless a neural model is later built
Architecture details are vision-specific

title: A Simple Neural Network Module for Relational Reasoning
signal_engine_relevance: Useful for modeling relations across speaker turns, analyst questions, management answers, and entities
Highlights relation-specific evaluation needs
core_idea: A simple module can reason over pairs of objects by aggregating learned relation functions.
historical_importance: It showed that explicit relational modules can solve tasks standard networks miss.
beginner_takeaway: Some questions are about relationships, not isolated objects or sentences.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Evaluate whether answer-evasion labels improve with Q/A pair features
Test relation features on analyst pressure examples
risks_limitations: Synthetic visual tasks differ from earnings calls
Relation extraction can create brittle pair explosions

title: Variational Lossy Autoencoder
signal_engine_relevance: Frames summarization and representation learning as controlled loss, not arbitrary compression
Useful for future transcript abstraction experiments
core_idea: Constraining the decoder can make latent variables carry useful global information.
historical_importance: It addressed a key failure mode in generative latent-variable models with powerful decoders.
beginner_takeaway: A summary should discard noise while preserving the information needed for the task.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Measure whether summaries preserve gold evidence spans
Compare abstraction levels for reviewer usefulness
risks_limitations: Generative modeling is not implemented
Lossy compression can hide legally/financially important nuance

title: Relational Recurrent Neural Networks
signal_engine_relevance: Good conceptual model for maintaining multiple transcript threads: guidance, risk, analyst pressure, and callbacks
Bridges memory and relation reasoning
core_idea: Memory can be represented as interacting slots, making recurrent models better at relational reasoning.
historical_importance: It connected memory-augmented sequence models with relation-centric computation.
beginner_takeaway: A call has several active threads; one hidden state may be too cramped to track them all.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Evaluate callback detection across sections
Track topic-thread state against human annotations
risks_limitations: Research model not implemented
Memory slots need labels or strong evaluation to be credible

title: Quantifying the Rise and Fall of Complexity in Closed Systems: The Coffee Automaton
signal_engine_relevance: Suggests measuring information dynamics over an earnings call rather than treating all sections equally
Useful for signal density timelines
core_idea: A simple automaton can model complexity rising and falling as two liquids mix toward equilibrium.
historical_importance: It operationalized the complexodynamics intuition in a concrete closed-system toy model.
beginner_takeaway: Complexity can be a time series; the most informative state may not be the beginning or end.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Compare signal density by call phase
Test whether Q&A complexity predicts review priority
risks_limitations: Toy physical model, not transcript semantics
Compression and complexity metrics require careful normalization

title: Neural Turing Machines
signal_engine_relevance: Inspires explicit memory/retrieval components for long transcripts instead of stuffing everything into one context
Relevant to RAG and persistent evidence stores
core_idea: A neural controller can learn to read and write from external memory using differentiable operations.
historical_importance: It was a landmark in memory-augmented neural networks and algorithmic task learning.
beginner_takeaway: Long reasoning often needs an external memory, not just a larger hidden state.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Evaluate retrieval memory hit rate
Audit whether generated summaries cite stored evidence
risks_limitations: Original NTM is hard to train and not a practical repo component
External memory needs transparent indexing and auditability

title: Deep Speech 2: End-to-End Speech Recognition in English and Mandarin
signal_engine_relevance: Guides future audio transcript quality and prosody roadmap without requiring paid APIs
Clarifies that ASR quality is a core dependency for audio-first signal claims
core_idea: A large end-to-end neural system can replace many hand-engineered speech recognition pipeline components.
historical_importance: It showed end-to-end ASR could work at scale across languages when paired with data and compute discipline.
beginner_takeaway: Speech intelligence starts with transcription quality, data scale, and measurable error rates.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Track ASR word error on any manually checked clips
Compare transcript-only vs transcript+prosody on reviewed labels
risks_limitations: Training ASR is out of scope
Audio claims require legally safe media and quality labels

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
signal_engine_relevance: Supports a disciplined 30/100/500 transcript roadmap and stops premature large-model training
Frames when more data matters more than model cleverness
core_idea: Language model loss follows predictable power-law trends with model size, data size, and compute over broad ranges.
historical_importance: It helped turn model scaling into an empirical planning discipline.
beginner_takeaway: More model is not automatically better; data, compute, and evaluation must scale together.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Plot learning curves for local baselines by transcript count
Pre-register evaluation gates before scaling
risks_limitations: Original results concern large LMs, not tiny finance classifiers
Later scaling-law work changed some optimal-data conclusions

title: A Tutorial Introduction to the Minimum Description Length Principle
signal_engine_relevance: Provides evaluation philosophy for choosing simple explainable models until evidence justifies complexity
Useful for weak-label and active-learning governance
core_idea: The best model can be viewed as the one that compresses data well, balancing model description and residual errors.
historical_importance: It is a foundational tutorial for information-theoretic model selection.
beginner_takeaway: A good explanation should make the data shorter without hiding mistakes.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Track errors saved per added feature
Compare deterministic rules vs learned models under a simplicity rubric
risks_limitations: The principle is conceptual unless converted into concrete metrics
MDL can be mathematically heavy for portfolio readers

title: Machine Super Intelligence
signal_engine_relevance: Useful mainly as a caution against overclaiming intelligence in Signal Engine 2.0
Encourages precise task definitions and bounded claims
core_idea: A theoretical study of universal artificial intelligence and superintelligent agents.
historical_importance: It influenced later AGI and DeepMind-era thinking about intelligence, capability, and safety.
beginner_takeaway: Big intelligence claims require formal definitions and careful limits.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Audit product language for unsupported AI claims
Separate tool assistance from validated reasoning ability
risks_limitations: Not an applied earnings-call paper
Theoretical framing can distract from concrete evaluation

title: Kolmogorov Complexity and Algorithmic Randomness
signal_engine_relevance: Deep foundation for compression-based novelty, boilerplate, and signal-density ideas
Supports honest uncertainty around what compression metrics can and cannot prove
core_idea: Algorithmic information theory studies the shortest descriptions of objects and formal notions of randomness.
historical_importance: It provides the mathematical background behind MDL, complexity, and randomness discussions on the list.
beginner_takeaway: Random-looking text can be hard to compress but still useless; complexity needs task context.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Validate compression metrics against human labels
Check false positives on boilerplate and legal disclaimers
risks_limitations: Book-level theory, not an implementation
Kolmogorov complexity is uncomputable in general

title: Stanford's CS231n Convolutional Neural Networks for Visual Recognition
signal_engine_relevance: Training-ground reference for future multimodal feature extraction and model-card literacy
Useful to keep visual/audio claims grounded in fundamentals
core_idea: A practical course resource for understanding and training convolutional neural networks for visual recognition.
historical_importance: CS231n educated a generation of deep learning practitioners and tied theory to implementation practice.
beginner_takeaway: Before using visual features, understand data, architecture, optimization, and error analysis.
possible_evaluation_ideas: Require visual feature coverage reports
Compare multimodal lift with human-reviewed decision tasks
risks_limitations: Course resource, not a single paper
Visual recognition is only indirectly relevant to transcript-first earnings calls
